sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: h1, two editions of the ONS nation rates printed in two documents, projected by the Guide's "keep changing by the same amount" shape. Medium target (no Easy slot); measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 3 L68-76 gives 2021 (England 13, Scotland 14.8, Wales 14.1, NI 13.8); Doc 1 L42-50 gives 2022 (England 12.7, Wales 14.1, NI 14.0, Scotland 13.9). Changes: Scotland -0.9, England -0.3, Wales 0, NI +0.2. Scotland: 13.9 - 0.9 x 9 = 5.8 (2031), 13.9 - 0.9 x 10 = 4.9 (2032). England reaches 4.9 only in 2048; Wales and NI never.
- Universe: the four UK nations, each printed once per edition; Wales and NI excluded by their zero and upward changes, England by its later year (2048).
- Necessity: Doc 3 is the only source of 2021 nation rates (searched "14.8", "13.8%", "13% in England", "in Scotland"; Doc 4 L638 gives only UK 14.1% in 2019 and 13.3% in 2021 and says "Declines were seen across all constituent countries"); without it no nation's change can be formed. Doc 1 is the only source of 2022 nation rates (searched "12.7%", "13.9%", "14.0%"; Doc 2 L417 gives only UK 12.9% in 2022; D01 L188 "12.7%" is a population share by age); without it no change can be formed. The question supplies neither year's values. Recall risk: ONS nation rates for 2021 and 2022 may be remembered by a strong model; a removal probe per document is the concrete check (see Blind solve).
- Selected-lever checks: Calculate across documents: one change per nation needs both editions. Who belongs where: the 2021 list runs England, Scotland, Wales, NI; the 2022 list England, Wales, NI, Scotland; positional pairing gives Scotland 14.8 against 14.1 (-0.7) and 2035 (scratchpad aq02157_calc.py).
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Linking across documents) pairing by list position: 2035. Mode 2 (Figure that must be computed) 8.9 / 0.9 = 9.89 years rounded down: 2031, when Scotland is at 5.8. Mode 3 (Wrong jurisdiction or scope) UK aggregate 13.3 -> 12.9 (-0.4 a year) from 12.9: 2042. All recomputed. Considered and not declared: relative (percent) change, 2039, ruled out by "percentage-point change"; England alone, 2048; Doc 4's 2019-2021 UK pace (-0.4) applied to Scotland, 2045; counting from 2023, 2033.
- Calculation verification: Python Decimal 2026-10-08 (scratchpad aq02157_calc.py): Scotland first year 2032 (4.9) from 2022, and 2032 from 2021 (14.8 - 0.9 x 11 = 4.9); strict "below 5" also 2032. Every reasoning expression is exact in float (13.9 - 14.8 gives -0.9000000000000004, written as 14.8 - 13.9 = 0.9).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: the page overview gives only UK rates (12.9% Doc 1; 13.3% Docs 3 and 4; 12% Doc 5); no nation rate and no 2032 anywhere in the bundle. Shortest complete route: find both nation lists, match names, compute four changes, project Scotland.
- Precision/readings: answer is a whole year, no rounding. England's "13%" (no decimal) cannot change the answer: for any 12.95-13.05 England's first year is 2044-2053. Starting the projection from 2021 or 2022 gives the same year. "5% or below" and "below 5%" both give 2032 (4.9). Doc 5 L88's Scotland 11% is maternal smoking at booking (2023), Doc 1 L60's NI 21.3% is youth vaping; neither is an adult smoking rate.
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (notes/intake.json; caller read all five documents).
- Style/set review: 23 words, no em dashes. q02 uses Doc 1 and Doc 2 on a different topic (flavour-restriction methods); no shared facts or answer path.
- Warnings answered: pending preflight.

sections.question: If each UK nation's adult smoking rate repeated its 2021-to-2022 percentage-point change yearly, in what year would one first reach 5% or below?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source fact (Doc 3, ONS report Adult smoking habits in the UK: 2021): the adult smoking rate was 13% in England, 14.8% in Scotland, 14.1% in Wales and 13.8% in Northern Ireland.

Step 2. Source fact (Doc 1, ONS Adult smoking habits in the UK 2022): the rate was 12.7% in England, 14.1% in Wales, 14.0% in Northern Ireland and 13.9% in Scotland. This list gives the nations in a different order, so each nation is matched by name.

Step 3. Calculation (from Steps 1 and 2; Doc 3 and Doc 1): Scotland's yearly fall: 14.8 - 13.9 = 0.9 percentage points.

Step 4. Calculation (from Steps 1 and 2; Doc 3 and Doc 1): England's yearly fall: 13 - 12.7 = 0.3 percentage points.

Step 5. Calculation (from Steps 1 and 2; Doc 3 and Doc 1): Wales's change: 14.1 - 14.1 = 0, so repeating it never brings Wales down to five per cent.

Step 6. Calculation (from Steps 1 and 2; Doc 3 and Doc 1): Northern Ireland's change: 14.0 - 13.8 = 0.2 percentage points upward, so it never falls to five per cent either.

Step 7. Calculation (from Step 3; Doc 3 and Doc 1): Scotland's fall over nine more years: 0.9 * 9 = 8.1 percentage points.

Step 8. Calculation (from Steps 2 and 7; Doc 3 and Doc 1): Scotland's rate nine years after 2022: 13.9 - 8.1 = 5.8, still above five per cent.

Step 9. Calculation (from Step 3; Doc 3 and Doc 1): Scotland's fall over ten more years: 0.9 * 10 = 9 percentage points.

Step 10. Calculation (from Steps 2 and 9; Doc 3 and Doc 1): Scotland's rate ten years after 2022: 13.9 - 9 = 4.9, at or below five per cent for the first time.

Step 11. Calculation (from Step 4; Doc 3 and Doc 1): England's fall over the same ten years: 0.3 * 10 = 3 percentage points.

Step 12. Calculation (from Steps 2 and 11; Doc 3 and Doc 1): England's rate ten years after 2022: 12.7 - 3 = 9.7, still above five per cent, so Scotland is the first nation to get there.

Step 13. Calculation (from Steps 2 and 10; Doc 1 and Doc 3): the year Scotland first reaches five per cent or below: 2022 + 10 = 2032.

Why these are traps: Doc 3 lists 2021 rates as England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland; Doc 1 lists 2022 as England, Wales, Northern Ireland, Scotland, so pairing by position gives 2035.
